books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the account of Lowell mill workers in the course books. The facts are as stated in the books; the wording is original.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In the mill town of Lowell, Massachusetts, young women from farm families worked in textile mills, tending power looms for long hours in exchange for wages. Mill owners housed them in company boardinghouses and set rules for their conduct. Many of the women used their wages to help their families and to save for the future.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The Lowell mill workers described here most directly illustrate which feature of the Northern economy?

options.misconception: Background from the books: the mill women were free workers paid wages; enslaved labor worked the Southern plantations, not the Lowell mills.

options.text: small farming without hired help at home.
options.misconception: The women left their farms to work in mills; the passage describes factory work for wages, not farming at home.

options.text: free labor, workers paid wages for factory work.

options.misconception: Background from the books: the gold rush drew fortune seekers west in 1849; Lowell’s mills stood in Massachusetts, and their workers earned wages at looms.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the mill women were free workers paid wages; enslaved labor worked the Southern plantations, not the Lowell mills.
rationales.B: The women left their farms to work in mills; the passage describes factory work for wages, not farming at home.
rationales.C: Young women tending looms for wages, saving for the future, are the free-labor North in miniature: paid work, not enslaved work.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the gold rush drew fortune seekers west in 1849; Lowell’s mills stood in Massachusetts, and their workers earned wages at looms.
rationales.general:
1. Name the work: tending power looms in a Massachusetts mill.
2. Name the pay: wages, saved or sent home to the family.
3. Name the system: free labor, where workers sell their work for pay and keep the bargain.
Remember: wages are the mark of free labor; when a worker is paid, ask what the pay lets her do.
